subject: general
question: Before writing codes in a high level language, a ______ of a program helps in representing the basic functionality of the intended program.
solution:
The correct answer is __**pseudocode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Pseudocode:**

 
 
• Pseudocode is a high-level description of a program that uses plain language or a simplified syntax to outline the logic and structure of the intended code.
 
• It allows programmers to focus on the algorithmic steps without getting bogged down by the syntax of a specific programming language.
 
 
 
• **Original code:**
 
 
• This option refers to the actual code written in a high-level language.
 
• It is the final implementation of the program, which is executed by the computer.
 
• While original code is essential for executing the program, it is not the most suitable choice for representing the basic functionality of the program before writing actual code.
 
 
 
• **Small code:**
 
 
• "Small code" is not a commonly used term in programming.
 
• It is vague and does not specifically describe any stage or representation of a program.
 
 
 
• **Naïve code:**
 
 
• "Naïve code" is also not a standard term in programming.
 
• It could refer to code written by a novice programmer, which may lack efficiency or optimization.
 
• However, it does not represent a stage or technique used to represent the basic functionality of a program.
